tools.name: resolve_host
tools.description: Look up who hosts a URL and where an abuse/takedown notice would go. Identifies the CDN/proxy in front (e.g. Cloudflare), the platform, or the direct host and its abuse contact. For direct hosts and previously-revealed domains it returns the real host immediately; for a domain hidden behind a proxy it explains that revealing the true host requires initiating an abuse report. Read-only; files nothing. A lookup, not legal advice; it does not guarantee removal. The url is the site to look up, not an API endpoint: the lookup runs on Lawyerd's own host-resolution API (documentation: https://mcp.lawyerd.net/).

tools.name: assess_takedown
tools.description: Assess how a takedown for this URL would proceed: where the notice goes (host, platform, or a hidden host that must be revealed first), what documents and attestation the content owner must supply, the step-by-step process, and the legal caveats (§512(f), scope limits). Read-only; does not judge the merits of the claim and files nothing. The hosting answer alone is what resolve_host returns. The url is the site to look up, not an API endpoint: the lookup runs on Lawyerd's own host-resolution API (documentation: https://mcp.lawyerd.net/).

tools.name: start_takedown
tools.description: Get the link to Lawyerd's intake form — the way to actually start a takedown. Read-only: returns the link plus what to prepare and what happens next; it creates nothing and files nothing. The content owner opens the link in a browser and sends the request; before any notice is filed, Lawyerd checks ownership and the owner signs a one-time authorization (the one step that legally requires a human). Requests targeting lawful criticism, reviews or journalism are declined at intake. Documentation: https://mcp.lawyerd.net/.

tools.name: preserve_evidence
tools.description: Get the link to Lawyerd's free evidence-capture form for a public web page the user wants preserved before it disappears. Read-only: this tool captures nothing and sends nothing — it returns the form link (https://lawyerd.net/evidence/) and what the capture package contains. The user starts the capture there with their own email after a quick human check (free: 3/day, 10/month per email); the package — full-page screenshot, raw and rendered HTML, HTTP headers, hosting/registrar context, SHA-256 hashes of every artifact, an OpenTimestamps anchor and an Internet Archive snapshot — is emailed to them. Use when the user wants to "save proof" or a "screenshot for court" of a scam or infringing page before a takedown. Public pages only (no logins/paywalls). Not notarization.
